title: Smooth resolution of a quasi-split marked nodal tower and its Cartier sub-boundary
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $J$ a finite group acting on $F$ by field automorphisms. Let $d\geq0$ and let $T_d\xrightarrow{f_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_1}T_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$ be a $J$-equivariant tower of integral finite-type schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with compatible semilinear actions. Each $f_i$ is projective, flat and finitely presented [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], has nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], has smooth geometrically integral generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and satisfies the quasi-split condition [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres]: every singular point of each fibre and both normalization branches are rational over its base residue field. For each $i$ give finitely many disjoint sections in the relative smooth locus with $J$-stable union $M_i$. Put $Z_0=\varnothing$ and $Z_i=f_i^{-1}Z_{i-1}\cup|M_i|$, and assume $f_i$ is smooth over $T_{i-1}\setminus Z_{i-1}$. No triviality of point stabilizers on the fibre graph, branches or marked sections is assumed. There exist integral smooth projective $F$-schemes $S_i$, with $S_0=T_0$, semilinear $J$-actions, and equivariant projective birational surjections $r_i:S_i\to T_i$ [def-kun-projective] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For $i>0$ there is an equivariant map $S_i\to S_{i-1}$ making the squares with $f_i$ commute. Birational means inducing an isomorphism of dense opens and equality of function fields. Each $E_i=(r_i^{-1}Z_i)_{\rm red}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor over $F$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Every local ring of $S_i$ is regular, and the components of $E_i$ through a point have equations given by distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-regular-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Moreover, let $X$ be an integral scheme with a $J$-action, let $C\subset X$ be an invariant effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and let $a:T_d\to X$ be equivariant and dominant with $a^{-1}|C|\subseteq Z_d$. Then $( (a r_d)^{-1}C)_{\rm red}$ is an effective Cartier divisor consisting of a subset of the components of $E_d$, and is relative strict normal crossings over $F$. Empty markings and the empty Cartier divisor are allowed. For $d=0$ all modifications are identities.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, printed pp.149--150, successive projective modifications of the plurinodal tower and the relative smooth-pair remark; the reduced Cartier inverse image is a subdivisor of the marked boundary. This is the entire quasi-split tower resolution, with no stabilizer-triviality assumption. Local parameter/UFD verification is the argument extracted from returned parent Steps 3--4.

proof.text: First each $T_i$ is H-projective over $F$. Indeed $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}F=\mathbf P^0_F$ has an ample invertible sheaf. Inductively the projective-bundle morphism $f_i$ is H-projective because its target has an ample invertible sheaf; H-projective composition gives an H-projective embedding of $T_i$ over $F$, whose pulled-back twisting sheaf is ample. Thus every $T_i$ has an ample invertible sheaf. We now induct on $i$, constructing the asserted $S_i,r_i$, additionally keeping $r_i$ an isomorphism over $T_i\setminus Z_i$. Start with $S_0=T_0$, $r_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $E_0=\varnothing$. The spectrum of a field is regular, smooth and H-projective over itself, and the empty divisor satisfies all boundary conditions.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2, p.149, projectivity of the successive modifications; Stacks 087S lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective and 01WE lemma-H-projective-composition

proof.text: Suppose $S_{i-1},r_{i-1}$ are constructed. Form $W=T_i\times_{T_{i-1}}S_{i-1}$ with projections $g:W\to S_{i-1}$ and $q:W\to T_i$, and pull back the markings to $N$. Apply nodal birational base-change geometry with $S=T_{i-1}$, $D=Z_{i-1}$ and $t=r_{i-1}$. It gives integral Noetherian finite-type $W$, projective proper $g,q$, birational surjective $q$, the nodal, flatness, finite-presentation and generic-fibre properties for $g$, and disjoint smooth sections $N$. Write $E=E_{i-1}$ and $B=|N|\cup g^{-1}|E|$. Since $|E|=r_{i-1}^{-1}Z_{i-1}$, $B=q^{-1}Z_i$. The diagonal semilinear action preserves $B$.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2, p.149, successive base modification of a nodal curve; Stacks 02V6 morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-projective and 0C5B curves.tex lemma-base-change-nodal-family

proof.text: The smooth pair $(S_{i-1},E)$ and $g,N$ satisfy the marked nodal relative log-chart theorem: $g$ is proper, flat, finitely presented, nodal, and smooth off $|E|$, and $N$ consists of disjoint sections in its smooth locus. Consequently $U=W\setminus B$ is dense and the divisorial pair $(W,B)$ is fine saturated, log regular and log smooth over the trivial log field $F$. This statement requires neither stabilizer triviality nor perfection of $F$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 and proof, pp.70--71; X Lemma 2.2, p.149, smooth-pair-over-a-field refinement

proof.text: Apply equivariant log-smooth fan regularization to $(W,B)$ and its finite semilinear $J$-action. It produces $a:W_1\to W$, projective in the projective-bundle sense, birational, equivariant and isomorphic over $U$, with $W_1$ integral smooth finite type over $F$. Its reduced boundary $B_1=(a^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ has, etale locally at each geometric point, a smooth $F$-map to $\mathbf A^r_F$ pulling back $V(z_1\cdots z_r)$, with all $r$ branches passing through that point. These are exactly the chart hypotheses required in Step 5. It is effective Cartier by the free-characteristic regular-boundary theorem, applied to the final log regular stage with free characteristic monoids and triviality locus $a^{-1}U$. The whole action lifts with its group law, including permutations of branches.

Apply relative maximal-branch strictification to $(W_1,B_1)$ with its lifted action. Obtain $b:S_i\to W_1$, projective birational and equivariant, isomorphic off $B_1$, with $S_i$ integral regular smooth finite type over $F$ and $E_i=(b^{-1}B_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ relative strict normal crossings. The cited tower terminates with empty old strict transform and full boundary equal to its relative SNC accumulated boundary; a terminal one-branch Cartier blowup may be the identity. Its hypotheses allow self-intersections and arbitrary permutations of branches and impose no condition on point stabilizers. In particular they apply even if the original quasi-split fibres carry nontrivial graph actions.

Set $r_i=qab:S_i\to T_i$ and use $gab:S_i\to S_{i-1}$ as the tower map. Their square commutes by the fibre product identity. Projective-bundle composition applies over the Noetherian targets and makes both composites projective in that convention. Each of $a,b$ is proper, hence closed, and has image containing a dense open of its integral target, so it is surjective. Together with the base-change theorem for $q$, this gives surjectivity and birationality of $r_i$. For the dense-open assertion one can intersect the dense isomorphism opens for the three birational maps; their inverses identify the resulting nonempty opens and function fields. Above $T_i\setminus Z_i$, $q$ is an isomorphism because $r_{i-1}$ is one off $Z_{i-1}$, and $a,b$ are isomorphisms there. Reduction does not change support, hence $|E_i|=r_i^{-1}Z_i$. The targets $T_i,S_{i-1}$ have ample invertible sheaves by Step 1 and induction, so projective-bundle-to-H-projective and H-projective composition make $r_i$ H-projective and $S_i$ H-projective over $F$. The maps are equivariant by composition. This completes the induction.

proof.text: Every $S_i$ and every intersection of components of $E_i$ is smooth over $F$, so all their local rings are regular. We check the strict normal crossings boundary definition for $E_i$: its distinct reduced components and all their intersections $C_K$ (indexed by sets $K$ of components) are regular. At $z\in C_K$ put $A=\mathcal O_{S_i,z}$ and let $I$ be the stalk of the ideal of $C_K$. The quotient $A/I=\mathcal O_{C_K,z}$ is regular local, hence a domain, so $I$ is prime; by the relative definition, computed on an affine open and localized at $z$, its height is $|K|$. Every localization of $A$ is a local ring of $S_i$, hence regular, so $A$ is catenary by the regular-ring universal catenarity theorem. In the catenary local domain $A$ all saturated chains from $(0)$ to the maximal ideal have length $\dim A$; concatenating maximal-length chains $(0)\subset\cdots\subset I$ and $I\subset\cdots\subset\mathfrak m$, which are saturated, gives $\dim A=|K|+\dim A/I$, the codimension required by the boundary definition. The boundary parameter criterion yields $I_{E_i,x}=(t_1\cdots t_r)$ for distinct members of a regular parameter system of $A=\mathcal O_{S_i,x}$. The regular-local UFD theorem makes the $t_j$ prime. The minimal primes of this product are exactly $(t_j)$: a prime containing the product contains a factor, and distinct parameter primes are incomparable. Thus the components through $x$ have precisely these individual parameter equations. Off $E_i$ take $r=0$.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), p.118; Stacks 0BI9 definition-strict-normal-crossings, 0BIA lemma-strict-normal-crossings and 0AG0 lemma-regular-local-UFD

proof.text: For the final clause, let $a:T_d\to X$ denote the map in the statement and put $h=ar_d:S_d\to X$. Dominance sends the generic point of the integral source to that of the integral target and induces an injection of function fields. A local Cartier equation $c$ of $C$ is nonzero in $k(X)$; its image is nonzero in $k(S_d)$. Stalks on an integral scheme inject into its function field, so its pullback is a nonzero element of every source stalk where it is defined. Those stalks are domains, so this equation is a nonzerodivisor and $h^{-1}C$ is effective Cartier. Its support lies in $|E_d|$ by the given containment. At $x$, use the parameters of Step 7 and put $T=t_1\cdots t_r$. Its local equation $f$ is a unit in $A[1/T]$: its vanishing set there is empty, so it belongs to no maximal ideal. The UFD boundary factorization theorem gives $f=u\prod_jt_j^{a_j}$ with $a_j\geq0$. Consequently $\sqrt{(f)}=(\prod_{a_j>0}t_j)$, since the $t_j$ are pairwise nonassociate primes. The empty product is $1$.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2, p.149, last sentence: reduced inverse image is a subdivisor; Stacks 0AG0 lemma-regular-local-UFD and 0BI9 paragraph following definition-strict-normal-crossings

proof.text: Globally choose exactly the components of $E_d$ whose generic points lie in $h^{-1}|C|$. The factorization in Step 8 shows at each stalk that the reduced inverse image is the union of these components: a component occurs locally exactly when its prime factor divides a Cartier equation, equivalently when that equation vanishes at its generic point. Thus this union agrees scheme-theoretically with $(h^{-1}C)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and its local product equations are nonzerodivisors. It is effective Cartier. Its components and their intersections are a subfamily of those of $E_d$, so they remain smooth over $F$ of the required codimensions. It is therefore relative strict normal crossings. Its union is $J$-invariant because $h,C$ are equivariant. Empty markings cause no change in the induction; for empty $C$ all exponents are zero. For $d=0$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $Z_0=\varnothing$, so the stipulated containment forces the Cartier pullback to be empty and the construction is the identity.
